chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Murazim who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
It is upon you to pray in the mosques, to be good neighbors to the people, to bear testimony (when required), and to attend the funerals.
Indeed, you cannot do without the people. Not a single one of you is self-sufficient from the people throughout his lifetime, and the people inevitably need one another.

key_terms.إِقَامَةُ الشَّهَادَةِ: Bearing testimony — refers to giving witness in legal and social contexts when one has relevant knowledge; a communal obligation
key_terms.الْجَنَائِزُ: Funerals — attending janaza prayers is a communal obligation (fard kifaya) and a way of honoring the deceased and supporting the bereaved
key_terms.حُسْنُ الْجِوَارِ: Good neighborliness — one of the most emphasized social duties in hadith, covering not just physical neighbors but all those in close social proximity
key_terms.لَا بُدَّ: There is no escape / inevitably — an Arabic emphatic expression indicating the absolute necessity of something

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about social duties toward the community?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) exhorts his followers to fulfill four specific communal obligations: congregational prayer in mosques, good neighborliness, bearing testimony when required, and attending funeral prayers. He then provides the rational justification: human beings are inherently interdependent, and no one can live in isolation from the community throughout their life. This teaching was directed at the Shia community living under Abbasid rule, encouraging them to remain engaged with the broader Muslim community rather than retreating into sectarian isolation.
